key_insight: A single high-resolution turbulent realization contains enough repeating multiscale spatial structure to train a patch-based deep model that reconstructs unseen turbulent fields at extreme super-resolution factors.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-efficient turbulence surrogate modeling and flow reconstruction when fully resolved training data are scarce or expensive to obtain.
method: Train a WDSR network only on overlapping patches from one high-resolution 2D homogeneous isotropic turbulence snapshot.
Predict subgrid detail patchwise on unseen flows and stitch outputs with Hann-window-weighted overlap-add.
Benchmark against interpolation and WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 full snapshots.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful reconstruction at x32 and x64 super-resolution, with improved vortical structures, higher-wavenumber energy recovery, and better multiscale statistics than conventional interpolation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the degree of spatial redundancy in the flow, so the single-realization patch strategy may generalize less well to non-homogeneous or more transient turbulent regimes.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
